doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: Learning many tunes and jamming in Russia
summary: Palmer says knowing many tunes lets musicians connect across languages.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah. And I tell my students all the time, you know it’s important to know as many tunes as possible because you never know where you’re going to be. You can be on a session, at a jam session and somebody that you really admire could be in that audience and you want to play with them and so you come up and they say, “Hey let’s play a tune.” And they say, “Okay what’chu want to play?” You know? And they might call a tune that you know that you learned and it’s like okay, then you make that musical connection. Or you could be in a place, like I’ve been at jam sessions in Russia where people don’t speak English, I don’t speak any Russian, but you just whisper over [scats] they say, “Okay yes, ‘Stablemates.’” “Okay let’s play that.” And they say yeah, and so then we’d play that. So yeah, you know when they say it’s like music is the universal language. You know there’s a melodic language to it that really connects people. So yeah it’s important to be able to communicate that way.
